value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Stratham's residential solar customers this session; Eversource is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

permit_authority.value: Town of Stratham Department of Planning & Building Development
permit_authority.notes: New Hampshire's State Building Code (IRC/IBC/NEC with state amendments) is adopted statewide but administered locally by each city/town — the same MIXED model applying to Lebanon, NH, researched separately this session (see nh-grafton-lebanon-eversource). Stratham's own Department of Planning & Building Development is the local AHJ.

interconnection_url.notes: See the identical statewide New Hampshire net-metering framework notes on the Lebanon, NH record (nh-grafton-lebanon-eversource) — per the NH Department of Energy's own page, net metering is available to customers of Eversource, Liberty Utilities, NH Electric Cooperative, and Unitil, with a 100kW AC peak-capacity cap for residential/small commercial customers.

value.name: Completed and signed Residential Building Permit Application
Construction documents (1 paper and 1 electronic copy)
Copy of manufacturer's specifications, installation instructions, and signage/labeling details
Plot plan showing the array's location relative to zoning setbacks
Letter from an NH-licensed Structural Engineer after review of the existing roof and proposed mounting system, plus a roof plan and line diagram of the electrical system
Details on mounting structure construction, array supports, framing members, foundation posts/footings, and module attachment method (gravity/wind-uplift design)

required_documents.notes: Per the Town's own 'Solar Energy System Permit (Residential) Application Checklist.' Codes referenced: 2021 IRC, 2021 IBC, 2023 NEC, NFPA 1, NFPA 101, and Stratham Zoning Ordinance Section 5.13. Local design criteria: 115mph max wind speed, 50psf ground snow load, 4ft frost depth, 3000psi max assumable soil bearing capacity. Roof-mounted systems are permitted by right in all zoning districts. Ground-mounted systems are permitted by right ONLY if all 5 criteria are met: array ≤1,750 sq ft, rear yard only (no clear-cutting within 20ft of a boundary), ≥50ft from the front property boundary and ≥35ft from all other boundaries, compliant with wetlands/shoreland setbacks, and ≤12ft in height — otherwise a Conditional Use Permit from the Planning Board (with a public hearing and abutter notification) is required.

value: Multiple inspections are required, including but not limited to: footing/foundation, framing/structural upgrades, labeling, grounding, and rapid shutdown/disconnect

timeline_days.notes: The Town's own document states the Building Inspector is 'dedicated to providing a comprehensive review... within a reasonable timeframe' without stating a specific day count, and notes that complete applications (all forms submitted together, signed by an NH-licensed electrician) expedite review.

other_conditions: Roof-mounted solar is permitted by right in all of Stratham's zoning districts

By-right ground-mounted solar is capped at 1,750 sq ft, rear-yard-only, with 50ft front / 35ft other-boundary setbacks and a 12ft height limit — systems exceeding these require a Conditional Use Permit from the Planning Board
A separate building permit application is required if a new roof is being installed as part of the project
The 100kW AC figure recorded here reflects the statewide net-metering peak-capacity threshold for residential/small commercial customers, not a separate Town permit-eligibility limit

permit_fees.notes: The Town's own document directs applicants to a separate online Fee Schedule page rather than stating a specific dollar figure inline, and notes the total cost of construction (used to calculate the fee) must include electrical work costs — left null rather than estimated.

rebates.notes: No specific Stratham or statewide New Hampshire rebate dollar amount was independently confirmed from a primary source this session — left null rather than guessed.
